title: `let r = f x in r` is not a tail call in a function whose only local allocation is made by the compiler
summary: `let r = loop (n - 1) (acc + 1) in r` is not a tail call in native code when the function allocates on the local stack, and here the only such allocation is the comparison of two tuples, which the compiler puts there. The documentation gives this form as the way to make a call not a tail call; OCaml 5.4.0 runs the loop in constant stack.
cause: `lambda/simplif.ml` removes `let r = e in r` and leaves the call, marked `Rc_normal`, at the end of the region of the function.
